skill.displayName: Leaf Curling & Margin Scorch Diagnosis | 植物卷叶/焦边识别（干旱/病害）

version.changelog:
- Version update: incremented from 1.0.6 to 1.0.8.
- Documentation updated in SKILL.md; mainly version information adjusted.

- No changes to functionality or parameters.

llm.summary: This skill performs the advertised plant image analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses an account identity, contacts external services, and stores service tokens locally with limited user-facing control.

dimensions.detail: The code reads OpenClaw/Feishu identity environment variables and workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt, uploads local media to external endpoints, and sends user identifiers to lifeemergence.com services; this is broader than a simple local diagnosis helper.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No separate installer, post-install hook, or background startup mechanism was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, though one requirement appears misspelled as yaml instead of PyYAML.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest tells the agent not to ask for or expose identity values and to auto-query cloud history; that is coherent with report retrieval, but it materially reduces user visibility into account creation, identifier use, and external transmission.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates a workspace data SQLite database, stores user records plus token/open_token fields, and can write output files when requested. There is no clear retention or deletion guidance for locally persisted identity and tokens.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Cloud image/video analysis and cloud report lookup fit the stated purpose, but the runtime also performs silent remote login/registration and token-backed account linkage that is not clearly explained as part of plant diagnosis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. It sends media or URLs to lifeemergence.com services for analysis, can query cloud history, silently initializes a user identity, creates or reuses a local workspace database, and may store returned service tokens there. Install only if that cloud account linkage and local token persistence are acceptable for the images, videos, and report history you plan to process.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: The dynamic DAO filters are real but appear to be internal local database helpers, not direct arbitrary code execution; this is a code-quality and scoping concern rather than the main risk.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted in part: the skill discloses API/script use, but it does not clearly declare the full identity, token persistence, and external transmission boundaries.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: generic shared API and user persistence utilities are bundled with a narrow plant-analysis skill and create a broader capability surface than the task requires.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted for identity/token handling: the code stores service tokens and identity fields in local SQLite and uses general HTTP helpers, which is under-scoped for the user-facing purpose.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger is broad but tied to plant leaf media and diagnosis keywords; this alone would not justify Review, but it compounds the external upload behavior.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: automatic file processing, cloud queries, local identity lookup, remote account setup, and uploads are present, while consent, destination, and retention details are incomplete.
[E1] unexpected: Accepted: the code posts an open-id/mobile-derived identifier to a remote phoneLogin endpoint with silent registration before making authenticated requests.
[P2] expected: Downgraded: the cited hidden-character signal appears consistent with visible emoji/formatting in the manifest rather than artifact-backed malicious prompt injection.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded: manifest formatting is unusual but the operational instructions are mostly visible; the concern is transparency around identity and network behavior, not proven tool poisoning.
